subject.title: feat(models): make per-agent model allowlist explicit; aliases/defaults no longer restrict

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `modelPolicy.allow` as the durable public authorization contract for model overrides, with legacy default model maps migrated by doctor and config writes?
rationale: This is more than a mechanical regression repair: it adds a persistent default/per-agent configuration API, migration marker, and changed authorization semantics for existing users.

options.title: Adopt the explicit policy split
options.body: Keep `agents.defaults.models` metadata-only and accept `modelPolicy.allow` plus the one-time compatibility migration after current-head upgrade proof is attached.

options.title: Keep the legacy coupling
options.body: Reject the new public policy surface and retain the existing model-map authorization behavior, accepting the alias/default side effect.

options.title: Narrow before landing
options.body: Keep the direction but reduce the public surface or migration mechanism after owner review identifies a simpler compatible contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the explicit policy split
recommendation.body: Keep `agents.defaults.models` metadata-only and accept `modelPolicy.allow` plus the one-time compatibility migration after current-head upgrade proof is attached.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the active assignee and author of the proposed policy and migration design.
